newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares tread water in bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares tread water in bourse trade.

text.p: German carmakers were the stars of the show in early bourse trade on Friday, continuing a trend set on Thursday, with Volkswagen AG leading the posse after a warmly-received analysts' meeting on Thursday.
The DAX-30 index, which measures bourse trade in German blue-chip stocks, was slightly higher in early bourse trade, up 5.58 points, or 0.17 percent, at 3,357.07 points.
Volkswagen shares surged nearly 10 percent in early electronic trade, but came off slightly over the morning to stand at 1,084 marks, up 38 marks or 3.63 percent.
As bourse trade kicked off Volkswagen was up 115 marks, or 11.55 percent, at 1,115 marks, settling back to 1,088 marks, up 92 marks or 9.24 percent.

Europe's largest carmaker on Thursday kicked off 1997 by forecasting better first quarter earnings due to a 9.5 percent rise in sales, adding it expected higher profits and sales for the current year.
An analysts' meeting later in the day was warmly received and many auto analysts raised their EPS forecasts for the carmaker, boosting VW shares.

Other German carmakers were also lifted as the sector was in favour. Daimler-Benz AG was up 6.50 marks, 4.97 percent, at 137.20 Marks, BMW was up 11 marks. 0.75 percent, at 1,450 marks and Porsche was up 47 marks, 2.38 percent, at 2,020 marks.
"The Volkswagen group's figures were very convincing. Except for the cars today, the rest of the market is very quiet," said one Frankfurt trader.
Volumes were generally thin and dealers said they were waiting for new data before making a decision which course to take.
